routes.label: Split the region along the coordinate axes

question: A rectangular region is bounded by the graphs of the equations \(y=a,\) \(y=-b,\) \(x=-c,\) and \(x=d,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are all positive numbers. Which of the following represents the area of this region?
solution:
Since \(a,b,c,d\) are positive, the rectangle extends horizontally from \(x=-c\) to \(x=d\), and vertically from \(y=-b\) to \(y=a\). Its width and height are
\[
\text{width}=d-(-c)=c+d,
\]
\[
\text{height}=a-(-b)=a+b.
\]
Multiplying these lengths gives the area. Distributing each term of one factor across the other gives
\[
(a+b)(c+d)=ac+ad+bc+bd.
\]
Thus the area is \(ac+ad+bc+bd\), choice A.

solutionMethods.explanation:
Because all four parameters are positive, both coordinate axes pass through the rectangle. Cutting the region along these axes produces four smaller rectangles.

Above the \(x\)-axis, the height is \(a\); the widths to the left and right of the \(y\)-axis are \(c\) and \(d\). These two areas are \(ac\) and \(ad\). Below the \(x\)-axis, the height is \(b\), giving areas \(bc\) and \(bd\).

The four pieces cover the entire region and have no overlapping interiors, so their areas add:
\[
\text{area}=ac+ad+bc+bd.
\]
The answer is choice A.
